candidate_sentences.text: Operating cash flow was negative EUR 52.0 million as portfolio growth required funding, while year-end cash increased to EUR 39.1 million.

verified_key_information_units.information: Eleving Group achieved record-high revenue of EUR 250.0 million in 2025 (15.5% year-on-year increase), with EBITDA reaching EUR 101.9 million (13.5% increase) and net profit stable at EUR 29.2 million; the net portfolio grew 20.2% to EUR 446.3 million.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report '2025 at a glance'; Consolidated Statement of Profit and Loss and Other Comprehensive Income

candidate_sentences.text: Eleving Group delivered record revenue of EUR 250.0 million in 2025, up 15.4% from EUR 216.6 million in 2024.
Adjusted EBITDA rose 13.5% to EUR 101.9 million, while net profit from continuing operations increased modestly to EUR 29.2 million from EUR 28.8 million.
Total net profit was EUR 29.2 million, compared with EUR 29.6 million in 2024, when EUR 0.8 million came from discontinued operations.
Growth was supported by a 20.2% increase in the net portfolio to EUR 446.3 million and record loan issuances of EUR 458.0 million, up 24.3% year on year.

verified_key_information_units.information: Revenue breakdown shows traditional vehicle financing decreased 6.0% to EUR 67.0 million, flexible vehicle financing increased 25.9% to EUR 60.3 million, device financing contributed EUR 7.9 million (launched in 2025), and consumer lending grew 18.0% to EUR 114.8 million.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Keynote from the CEO section detailing business line contributions

candidate_sentences.text: Consumer lending generated EUR 114.8 million of revenue, up 18.0%; flexible vehicle finance generated EUR 60.3 million, up 25.9%; traditional vehicle finance contributed EUR 67.0 million, down 6.0%; and device financing contributed EUR 7.9 million following its launch in 2025.

verified_key_information_units.information: Strategic launch of installment loans in European markets (Latvia, Estonia, Romania, Armenia), generating EUR 14.7 million in loan issuances during 2025.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report sections on Operations in European markets and Business outlook

candidate_sentences.text: The Group introduced installment loans in Latvia, Estonia, Romania, and Armenia, generating EUR 14.7 million of issuances, and launched smartphone financing in Kenya and Uganda.

verified_key_information_units.information: Introduction of smartphone financing in Kenya and Uganda, building a EUR 13.5 million loan portfolio by year-end with 260 thousand customers.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Environmental information section and Management Report on Operations in African markets

candidate_sentences.text: The Group introduced installment loans in Latvia, Estonia, Romania, and Armenia, generating EUR 14.7 million of issuances, and launched smartphone financing in Kenya and Uganda.
By year-end, smartphone financing had reached a EUR 13.5 million portfolio and 260,000 customers.

candidate_sentences.text: Tanzania became the Group’s 17th market through motorcycle financing.

candidate_sentences.text: The Group also piloted AI voice agents at call centers, with capacity of up to 20,000 calls per day, and reported a reduced cost-to-income ratio.

candidate_sentences.text: A EUR 40 million bond tap was completed in March, followed in October by a EUR 275 million five-year senior secured bond issuance that refinanced EUR 150 million of bonds maturing in 2026.

candidate_sentences.text: A EUR 40 million bond tap was completed in March, followed in October by a EUR 275 million five-year senior secured bond issuance that refinanced EUR 150 million of bonds maturing in 2026.

details.completeness_justification: The candidate summary adequately covers most key information units: K1 (overall financial performance), K2 (revenue breakdown), K3 (installment loans), K4 (smartphone financing), K5 (Tanzania expansion), K6 (AI voice agents), K7 (bond tap), K8 (bond refinancing), K9 (dividends), and K12 (post-period funding). However, it omits the core material meaning of K10 (impairment expense details) and K11 (regulatory challenge in Moldova), both of which are HIGH importance and change the overall financial and risk picture. The absence of these two items results in a 'Generally yes' rating, as the main picture is captured but significant material risks and financial adjustments are missing.
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary is internally coherent with no material contradictions or logical gaps. All statements are consistent with each other, and the relationships between figures and explanations follow logically. The structure progresses logically from revenue and profit performance to specific business drivers, geographic expansion, funding activities, and capital structure changes. There are no self-contradictions, logical gaps, or organizational issues that would reduce coherence. While there is a minor numerical discrepancy between S2 and S3 regarding net profit figures (S2 states net profit from continuing operations increased modestly to EUR 29.2 million, while S3 states total net profit was EUR 29.2 million compared with EUR 29.6 million in 2024), this is clarified by S3's explicit mention of discontinued operations, which resolves any apparent inconsistency. The summary maintains clear internal logic throughout.
